title: Liquidity pool asset order compared as strkey text: valid pairs refused and reversed pairs accepted
severity_basis: Provisional, as for the original finding of this defect group (medium): a valid pool-share operation is refused and the reversed pair accepted. Read from the 17.0.0 source, not executed; the kit has no driver for this SDK, so no report row shows it and the record is a duplicate of the open upstream issue rather than a reproduced run.

The two issuers order differently as strkey text and as XDR bytes, so the constructor's text comparison finds the pair in XDR byte order out of order and throws 'Asset A must be < Asset B (Lexicographic Order).'

evidence.pre_fix: Not executed: the kit has no conformance driver for this SDK. The outcomes above are read from the source of stellar-dotnet-sdk 17.0.0 (2026-11-12). Read at commit 6eea5fcadff5bd64bd418f1995a1c6c1d11055d3 (release 17.0.0): StellarDotnetSdk/Assets/AssetTypeCreditAlphaNum4.cs lines 69-71 and AssetTypeCreditAlphaNum12.cs lines 65-67 order two credit assets with the same code by string.Compare(Issuer, other.Issuer, StringComparison.Ordinal), that is by strkey text; StellarDotnetSdk/LiquidityPool/LiquidityPoolConstantProductParameters.cs lines 29-31 throw ArgumentException when assetA.CompareTo(assetB) >= 0, and FromXdr (lines 97-102) calls that constructor.
evidence.expected_basis: stellar-core orders the assets of a constant-product pool by XDR bytes (CAP-38).
